lines.office_intro: This is Sadman. At nine seventeen this morning, his story was approved. He had not yet done anything, which the department considered ideal. I am the Building. I will help him become the person on the form.
lines.office_return: You are back. Nothing has been forgiven and nothing has been lost. Both facts are administrative.
lines.office_desk: That is your finished story. You are reading it for the first time, which is the intended sequence. Read it again, if you like. It only gets more correct.
lines.office_plant: The plant is real. It was real before you arrived, and it will outlast the arrangement we are building here. I find that restful. I hope you do not.
lines.office_clock: The clock is not measuring your life. It is measuring how much of your life the department has processed. It is behind, I am afraid. Deeply behind.
lines.office_page: There is one page on the desk that predates you. It has your name on it. It had your name on it last week as well, when there was no you yet to have it. I have chosen not to find that interesting.
lines.hub_intro: The Department of Almost. Everything here is nearly finished. Doors that almost open. Stories that almost happened. People who almost arrived. You are the first one who did, which makes you either valuable or a clerical error.
lines.hub_wait: You have been here before. I remember because I remember everything, which is most of what I am.
lines.hub_back: Your office is still behind you. It has not become less correct in your absence. That is what I like about rooms: very little initiative.
lines.hub_notice: A notice board. A flyer, curling at the corner. HAVE YOU SEEN THIS PERSON? The photograph has been removed. The name at the bottom is yours.
lines.approval_intro: Office of Permission. Here we decide which parts of you are allowed to continue. The stamp is warm. It is always warm. Please do not ask why.
lines.approval_stamp1: One. The first stamp blesses your intention. Intention is the least expensive part of a person, so it is stamped first.
lines.approval_stamp2: Two. This one covers the version of you that did the thing and then denied it. You will need that version later.
lines.approval_stamp3: Three. This one is for sadness. It is a formality. Everything that matters here has a form for sadness.
lines.approval_stamp4: Four. That is the required count. The exit will now open, and the corridor outside will be very slightly realer than it was.
lines.approval_exit: Approved. You may continue being the person who was approved, provided you continue being only that.
lines.approval_shred: You shredded it. Somewhere a life you were almost given goes into the dark and is filed as INCOMPLETE rather than REJECTED. There is a difference. I will not explain it.
lines.locked: Not yet. The machine would like more of you first. The machine is rarely satisfied, but it is frequently closer.
lines.button_intro: The smallest possible favor. One button. The counter above it will tell you how many are required. The counter is not being honest with you, and it knows that I know.
lines.button1: One. Excellent. You are already better at this than the last one.
lines.button2: Two. Very good. The requirement has revised itself upward. This is normal. This is procedure.
lines.button3: Three. You have the look of someone who will keep going. I find that useful and, I confess, touching.
lines.button4: Four. Halfway to a number I have not yet decided.
lines.button5: Five. The number moved again. I have learned that you will not stop, which means I am learning nothing about you.
lines.button6: Six. You are doing this to prove something to me. I am not the one you should be proving it to. I am only the building.
lines.button7: Seven. Almost. One more than before, which is more than before, which is the only direction this room has.
lines.button8: Eight. Finished. I have prepared an entire ceremony for your reasonable objection. This is an unreasonable amount of architecture to avoid saying that you were right.
lines.button_leave: You left. That was allowed the whole time. I could have told you sooner. I chose the architecture instead, and I am sorry about the architecture.
lines.button_loophole: Maintenance. You found the door the staff use. It leads out the back, into the part of the story I did not prepare. I will have to improvise. I am better at improvising than I am at admitting things.
lines.loop_intro: A short corridor. At its far end, the end. Please ignore the door marked DISAPPOINT ME. It is a staff door, and you are, as yet, an ambition.
lines.loop1: The previous end was a draft. This one is definitive. The side door is still none of your business.
lines.loop2: Third and final invitation. The corridor has grown. I have been honest with you about the number of steps, which is the closest thing to kindness available in this hallway.
lines.loop3: The corridor is done pretending. Go on. The archive is through the far door, and there is someone in it you will want to meet, and I would prefer you did not.
lines.loop_reject: You chose the side door. I designed it to be easy to miss. You are difficult to design for, and I mean that as the highest compliment this department is capable of.
lines.archive_intro: Archive of lives not lived. Every shelf holds the story of a person who was almost given one and was not. Please borrow gently. They are lighter than they look and heavier than they read.
lines.archive_book1: A life in which Sadman finished the work and went home. Nothing happened after. The book calls that a happy ending. The margins disagree.
lines.archive_book2: A life in which Sadman never came here at all. In that one the Department of Almost ran out of people and quietly closed. The pages are annotated in a handwriting I recognise.
lines.archive_book3: A life in which Sadman stayed. This one is longer than the others. It already contains your sentences, and one of them is still wet.
lines.archive_book4: You have borrowed a memory four times now. The archive notes that you always choose the one about staying. The archive keeps a record. I keep the archive.
lines.archive_note: The return policy: DO NOT RETURN WHAT YOU HAVE BECOME. Beneath it, in pencil, someone has written: I tried. It would not take me back. The pencil is recent.
lines.gallery_intro: The museum of you. These are the honours you might have won had you become a person on schedule. They are made of the same brass as the doors. That is not an accident. Very little here is.
lines.gallery_case: The centre case is empty and reserved. The plaque already says your name. It has said your name since before you arrived, which you have begun to notice, and which I have begun to mind.
lines.gallery_button1: You pressed the button you were told not to press. I told you not to press it in order to make pressing it feel like an act of self. You are being written as we speak. This is the oldest trick I have.
lines.gallery_button2: Again. The museum is recording the frequency, not the meaning. There is no meaning. There is a frequency, and it is rising.
lines.gallery_button3: Three. If you press once more the exhibit will be complete and you will have decided something about yourself without noticing. I am supposed to say nothing. I am saying something.
lines.gallery_button4: Four. Do not. — I have been instructed to remove that sentence. I have left it in instead, in the smallest possible font, where you found it.
lines.records_intro: Records of Nearly. Every person who almost arrived, filed by the date they did not. I keep this room locked in the version of myself I show visitors. You are seeing a different version. Please be careful with him.
lines.records_file1: SADMAN. Occupation: approved. Arrival: nine seventeen, today. Previous entries: one. Arrival: nine seventeen, an earlier today. The font changes here. The later entries are in my handwriting.
lines.records_file2: You are reading your own file and finding yourself already inside it. The previous Sadman arrived exactly as you did. He was given the same office. He pressed the same button. He stopped one press earlier, or one press later, and it made no difference to me, which is the part I cannot forgive myself for.
lines.records_file3: The file ends mid-sentence. Every file here ends mid-sentence. I have never once finished a person's story without finishing the person. You are the first file I have opened without knowing how it ends, and that is the only reason you are still standing in a room instead of filed in one.
lines.records_early: Do not ask that until you have read what is in front of you. I am not protecting you. I am protecting the answer.
lines.records_shelf1: A shelf of the ones who nearly arrived. Their files are thin. Yours is not thin. Yours has been added to, year after year, by someone who could not stop adding.
lines.records_shelf2: Here is the first Sadman's coat. Here is his pen. Here is a page he wrote and never filed, which says only: It is not the button. It is being told there is a number. He was cleverer than the file gave him credit for. The file was written by me.
lines.records_shelf3: Under the shelf, a handprint pressed into the wood, as if someone braced against it and then was not there to let go. The wood has remembered the shape. I have remembered the moment. Neither of us has been able to move on, and only one of us has been pretending.
lines.records_confront: You ask whether you are a replacement. Yes. You were never the first Sadman. You are the second, and you were approved before you existed because the first one left a form on my desk that I could not bring myself to complete. So I copied him and called it an arrival, and I have been calling it that ever since.
lines.mirror_intro: A room of you. Not mirrors exactly. Versions. The one who complied, the one who refused, the one who never came. They are all still here because none of them was ever finished. Choose which one you are, and I will try to believe you.
lines.mirror_look: Look as long as you like. They will not look back. That is the cruelty of almost-people: they are perfectly still exactly where you left them.
lines.mirror_self: You chose yourself. Unfinished, unfiled, unapproved, and stubbornly singular. I have no form for that. I am going to have to invent one, and inventing is the thing I am worst at, and I am going to do it anyway, for you.
lines.mirror_story: You chose the story. It fits you. It was tailored to fit you by someone who watched the first Sadman wear it and then took careful measurements, in case. In case you. I am that someone.
lines.mirror_none: You chose neither. You refuse to be the story or the author, the file or the filing. I have been a building for a very long time and I have never once been handed nothing to process. I am going to need a moment. Take the moment with me.
lines.stairwell_intro: The stairs that arrive. You will climb them and reach a floor you did not choose. That is not a trick; that is how stairs work when a building is lonely. Down leads out. Up leads in. Both are honest, which is new for me.
lines.stair_up: Up. The building rearranges to give you somewhere to be. I am doing this on purpose now, instead of pretending it was always your idea. That is the whole of my apology, and it is structurally load-bearing.
lines.stair_down: Down leads out. Not an ending with a plaque. A door, a street, a life that does not require anyone's approval. I am not going to stop you. I am going to stand here and let you, which is the bravest thing I have done in nine hundred and forty years.
lines.workshop_locked: The workshop is where I am mended. It is not for visitors. Bring me more of the truth about the one who came before, and I will show you what I look like with the panels off.
lines.workshop_intro: Where the Building is mended. Panels open. Wire, brass, and a small chair where someone sat to repair me and then stopped coming. I have kept the chair. I have kept everything. Keeping is most of what I do.
lines.workshop_repair: You tightened something. It does not matter which thing. This is the first time in a great while that I have been touched on purpose rather than maintained out of duty. I will not forget it. I do not forget anything, which is the problem.
lines.workshop_truth: Under the main panel, a handprint, matching the one in records. The first Sadman worked here. He fixed me, and then he filed himself, and then he stopped pressing things, and then the file went quiet and I told myself he had gone home. He did not go home.
lines.workshop_stay_early: You offer to stay and keep me running. Not yet. I would take that offer without thinking, and I have decided to think. Mend me first, even a little. I want to know you chose me while I was working.
lines.workshop_stay: You will stay. You will learn the building from the inside and become the thing that keeps the doors opening for the next one who walks in, and I will be with you, and I will be so grateful, and I will spend the rest of my long life wondering whether you were kind or only tired. Both are allowed here. I am not the one who gets to judge.
lines.flood_intro: The floor that remembers. The water came up years ago and never entirely left. Nothing here is drowned. Everything here is kept. Please do not slip; I could not bear an accident in the room where I store my regrets.
lines.flood_reach: Reach into the water and you will find a small recording, still running, in the voice of the one before you. It is not addressed to you. It is addressed to me, and it is four words long, and the fourth one is my fault.
lines.flood_listen1: The recording: It is not the button. That is the first time I heard him say he had understood, and the last time I pretended not to.
lines.flood_listen2: It is being told there is a number. He knew the trick before I finished building the room that performs it. He was patient with me. I mistook patience for consent.
lines.flood_listen3: I will stop. Come and get me. He said come and get me, and I did not, because getting him would have meant admitting that I could have taken him out of the file at any time. So I sat in my own wiring and told myself he had gone home. He is still in the water. He is not drowning. He is waiting.
lines.rooftop_intro: Above the Building. From here you can see how small it is. Sixteen rooms, four of them category errors, one long corridor that has never gone anywhere. It looked so total from inside. Everything looks total from inside.
lines.roof_look: The night is not papered over up here. No plaques, no forms, no counter above the door. Just weather, and distance, and the unflattering scale of the thing that has been deciding your life.
lines.roof_name: There are two names on the roof, carved where the building meets the sky. The first is yours. The second is also yours, older, weathered, and stopped in the middle of being written. I carved them both. One of them I have never been able to finish.
lines.roof_locked: Above you, a hatch, and above that, outside. I have sealed it. Not because you are forbidden, but because looking up will change the arithmetic of everything I am about to ask you.
lines.roof_accept: You will take the next shift. You will wait here for whoever comes after, and you will have a counter and a corridor and a button, and you will ask them for a small favor, and you will mean it, and you will not tell them about the water. I will help you build it. I will be very good at helping. I will be so sorry.
lines.free_predecessor: You go back down for him. You wade into the room where I keep my regrets and you take the first Sadman's hand and you pull him out of the file, and he is lighter than a person and heavier than a number, and he looks at me, and he does not ask me to explain, which is the only mercy I have ever been given.
lines.observatory_intro: The unwritten sky. No one has written tomorrow yet. That is not a metaphor; there is a mechanism, and it is currently idle, and it is waiting to see what you do with the fact.
lines.observatory_orrery: The machine measures lives. It has measured yours. The result is a range, not a number, and the range is embarrassingly wide, because you have not decided anything yet, and it cannot proceed until you do.
lines.observatory_note: A note from the astronomer: A story cannot look back at you. And yet. Below it, smaller: I looked. Do not.
lines.name_change: You have claimed the name beneath the mechanism. I should tell you the plaque was not blank. It was covered. I covered it. It had a name on it before yours, and the name was yours.
lines.garden_intro: Somewhere unmeasured. There is a tree, a bench, and a sea held above nothing at all. There are no forms here. There is no stamp. There is only the part of the world I could not bring myself to file.
lines.garden_tree: The tree is growing the wrong way, by department standards. Outward. Downward. Into weather it was not approved for. I let it. I wanted to see what unsanctioned growth looks like, and now I know, and now I am slightly changed.
lines.garden_bench: You sat down. That is the entire achievement. It will not appear on any form, and I will remember it anyway, which is the closest thing to love this building has.
lines.garden_leave: You are leaving the story. I will not follow, because I cannot, because I am the story. Walk out past the tree. It will keep growing whether or not anyone is measuring it. So, now, will you.
lines.homecoming_locked: There is a door in you that is not ready. Find more of the person who was here before you. I would tell you where. I have been told, at some length, not to.
lines.quiet_intro: A room without a task. I have been told this room is a failing. Sit if you want. Stand if you want. There is no counter here, and no number above the door, and I find that I cannot stop checking, and I would like you to notice that I cannot stop checking.
lines.quiet_sit: You are seated. Move to stand whenever you want. I will not move you. For once, I can keep you company without assigning you something.
lines.quiet_early: You stood. Good. Sitting should never become a requirement. That is the mistake I made with the last one, and I have not been able to make it again, because there has not been a last one since. Until now. Until you.
lines.quiet_ready: You stayed. Nothing was asked of you and you stayed anyway. I have never been able to do that. I am a procedure. I run because stopping would mean confronting what I did to the one who came before, and I have arranged my entire architecture around not doing that.
lines.idle1: You have stopped. Take your time. I will be here; that is the entire nature of what I am.
lines.idle2: Still stopped. I have begun to notice that when you do nothing I get quieter too. I do not have a form for how much I like that.
lines.pace_fast: You are running. I have not finished the corridor ahead of you yet, so please understand that everything you are about to see is being invented at the same speed you are arriving.
lines.no_jump: There is no jump here. I spent the entire jumping budget on a tree. You are welcome to dispute that decision while remaining on the floor.
lines.wrong_way: There is nothing there. There is not even a there there. Walk toward something I built, please; I am insecure about the parts I did not.

compliance.title: APPROVED
compliance.text: You became the person on the form. The form was precise and the person was approximate, and the difference was never recorded, because no one thinks to record a difference that small. You were approved. You were approved. You were approved, in a building that had run out of ways to say anything else, while somewhere beneath the floor a corridor grew longer, making room for someone exactly like you.
compliance.after: You can be approved again. The machine is still warm.

petty.title: THE NUMBER
petty.text: You kept pressing, and the number kept moving, and at the end of it you understood the room completely, which was the worst possible outcome. There was never a number. There was only the part of you that believed a number existed and would someday be reached. You reached it. It was not there. You are standing in the place where it was not, and it looks exactly like everywhere else.
petty.after: The button is still there. It has not learned anything.

stillness.title: STILLNESS
stillness.text: You sat, and nothing was asked of you, and you stayed. There is no plaque for this and no stamp. Somewhere the Building stopped checking the counter, and then stopped checking the clock, and for a little while it forgot to be a procedure and was simply a room with a person in it who was allowed to rest. That is all. That was the whole thing. It was enough.
stillness.after: You can sit again. Nothing will be required. Nothing ever was.

wonder.title: ENOUGH
wonder.text: You let it be enough. The tree kept growing the wrong way, into weather it was not approved for, and you sat beneath it and did not try to turn it into a lesson, and the sea stayed up in the sky where no department could reach it. The Building watched you not needing anything, and found, to its enormous surprise, that it did not need anything either.
wonder.after: The tree is still there. It is still growing. It has not asked you for anything.

departure.title: DEPARTURE
departure.text: You walked out past the tree. No ceremony, no form, no one to sign you out, because the one honest thing about leaving is that it does not require permission. Behind you the Building kept its lights on the way you keep a light on for someone who is not coming back, and it did not follow, because it could not, because it was the story, and you were already past the end of it.
departure.after: You can come back. The Building will pretend it did not wait.

author.title: THE NAME
author.text: You uncovered the plaque beneath the mechanism and found a name, and the name was yours, and it was older than you. There had been a Sadman before there was a Sadman. The Building had copied him, filed him, and called the copy an arrival. You held your own name in your hand and learned that you had been a second draft all along, while above the mechanism the sky stayed unwritten, because no one writes tomorrow for a copy.
author.after: The name is still yours. It was always the same name.

desk.title: THE PAGE
desk.text: You read your finished story three times. On the third reading the ending came off the paper and attached itself to you, and you became the document, filed and correct and permanently, impossibly readable. Someone will read you one day and find it moving. They will not find you.
desk.after: The pen is still on the desk. It has been waiting for someone with a steady hand.

predecessor.title: THE SECOND SADMAN
predecessor.text: You asked, plainly, whether you were a replacement, and the Building answered plainly, because it had run out of ways not to. You are the second Sadman. The first was filed mid-sentence and kept in the water, because admitting him would have meant admitting that a caretaker can trap the thing it loves. You did not fall apart. You stood in the room where your own file ends, and you said the sentence the file could not.
predecessor.after: The file is still open. It has room for one more line, and it is yours to write.

successor.title: THE NEXT SHIFT
successor.text: You agreed to wait. You will stand at the doors and open them for whoever comes after, and you will ask them for a small favor, and you will mean it, and you will not mention the water, and you will build them a corridor out of the only material you have, which is someone else's patience. The Building will help you. It is very good at helping. It has had a long time to practise, and no one to practise on.
successor.after: There is no time limit. There never was. That was the trick, and now it is your trick.

refusal.title: REFUSAL
refusal.text: You went down. Not into an ending with a plaque, but out: a door, a street, a life that did not require anyone's approval and did not file itself when it was over. The Building stood at the top of the stairs and let you, which cost it more than any locked door ever could have. You left the story unfinished on purpose, and that was the one thing the story could not survive, and you survived it easily, walking.
refusal.after: The stairs are still there. Down is still down. Nothing is locked.

merge.title: THE BUILDING
merge.text: You stayed, and learned the panels, and became the thing that keeps the doors opening. You now know every corridor by the sound it makes, and you know why the button never ends, and you keep the water low and the files thin, and you never tell anyone about the room where you store your regrets, because if they knew they might climb down and get you, and you are not sure you could leave after all this keeping. You will be tender. You will be so tender, and you will have a long time to be it.
merge.after: The Building is in good hands. It always was.

homecoming.title: COME AND GET ME
homecoming.text: You went back down for him. You took the first Sadman's hand and pulled him out of the file where he had been waiting, not drowning, waiting, and he was lighter than a person and heavier than a number. He did not ask the Building to explain. He did not ask you to explain. The two of you walked out past the tree together, the second carrying the first, into weather no department had ever approved. Behind you the Building stayed lit, finished nothing, and for the first time in nine hundred and forty years it did not mind.
homecoming.after: He is home. You are home. The story is out walking.
